title: Captain playbook: Garden/Business selectable Slack theme implementation (gd-XFizxz9y3Y)
description:
# Captain playbook: Garden/Business selectable Slack theme (gd-XFizxz9y3Y)

You are driving plan epic gd-XFizxz9y3Y to closure: implement the selectable
Garden/Business Slack card theme system against gardenio's real bridge code.

## Design is locked — do not redesign

The full design (glyph tables, palette, avatar, accessibility rule, and the
selection mechanism) is written up in the repo at
`gardenio/plans/slack-greenhouse-restyle.md` on branch
`agent/slack-greenhouse-restyle/gd-pALXjDaPK8` (PR #186) — read that file
first, it is the spec. Do not re-litigate glyph choices (Task is 🌱, not 🌰 —
this was explicitly reverted once by the operator) or invent a different
selection mechanism. If something in the spec is genuinely ambiguous for
implementation, resolve it yourself per Rule 6 of the captain-authoring-guide
(you own forks in your own lane); only escalate if it's a real cross-cutting
or privilege-gated question.

## What to build

Three phases are already broken into steps under gd-XFizxz9y3Y
(`gb plan show gd-XFizxz9y3Y` or `kd list --parent gd-XFizxz9y3Y`):

1. **Theme module + config wiring** — a `Theme` struct (glyph table, palette,
   avatar) with `Garden` and `Business` instances in a new `theme.go`; env
   parsing for `SLACK_CARD_THEME` / `SLACK_CARD_THEME_BUSINESS_CHANNELS`
   mirroring the existing `linkUnfurlChannels`/`SLACK_LINK_UNFURL_CHANNELS`
   pattern in `gardenio/controller/internal/bridge/bot.go` +
   `link_unfurl.go`; helm chart + deploy-values plumbing
   (`cardTheme`/`cardThemeBusinessChannels` under `slackBridge.slack`).
2. **Card rendering wiring** — thread every literal glyph/color currently
   inline in `bot_agents.go`, `bot_agents_wrapup.go`, `link_unfurl.go`,
   `agentstream.go` through a `themeFor(channel)` lookup instead.
3. **Tests + rollout** — update the 9 existing card tests for the Garden
   default, add Business-mode coverage, then flip
   `cardThemeBusinessChannels` for one volunteer channel in
   `deploy-values/gardenio-k3s.yaml` and confirm in Slack.

## Landing the work

- Branch per change, PR against `main` on GitHub (this repo's remote is
  GitHub, not GitLab — `gb mr link` will reject the PR URL; record it with
  `kd comment add <bead-id> "PR: <url>"` instead).
- `make build`, `make test`, `make lint`, `helm lint gardenio/helm/gardenio/`
  before every PR (root `CLAUDE.md` "Landing the Plane").
- Close each step bead as its change lands; this captain's terminal goal is
  all of gd-XFizxz9y3Y's children closed.
- Keep the two themes' glyph-collision/accessibility rules intact — every
  inline glyph stays glued to its verbal label in the same text run, exactly
  as documented in the plan doc's "Accessibility rule" section.

title: Blocked by a lane/privilege: file an escalation, not just a comment
description: BLOCKED BY A LANE OR PRIVILEGE? FILE AN ESCALATION (operator policy 2026-10-12, gd-ltxJaVRLWT). If a task needs something you are barred from or cannot do (edit gardenio/helm/**, deploy-values/**, terraform, RBAC/ServiceAccounts, secrets, ziti, or any privileged action), do not just comment and stop: write exactly what is needed on the task AND file a concrete 'gb escalation create' (--requesting-task <task-id>, --operation-type describing the action, --context with the exact change and acceptance) so the privileged owner/operator has a durable handle. A comment alone is not enough. Use a decision bead only for a genuine fork between divergent options (e.g. 'should we allow X at all'); use an escalation when the action is known and someone with the right access must do it. This supersedes the 'comment + decision bead' instruction in the LANES section of gd-oI2AIaSzjF.

title: gb wait ci: --repo is the current owner/name (mattbakerconsulting/gardenio)
description:
gb wait ci --repo takes the repo's CURRENT owner/name: mattbakerconsulting/gardenio, not joyousaversion/gardenio. Read it from `git remote get-url origin`.

The sequence stays push, `gb wait ci --repo <owner/name> --sha "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`, `gb stop` (crew-survival advice gd-L4MSFKLoV5 item 1). The wait is matched on `repository.full_name` from GitHub's workflow_run deliveries, folding only case. The repo moved from joyousaversion to mattbakerconsulting, so a wait keyed on the old name never matches a delivery. It is then resolved only by the 5-minute Actions poll or the 25-minute stop timer, not about a minute after CI concludes. The sha must be the full 40 characters. How the wait resolves and how to diagnose one that did not wake: gardenio/docs/triggers.md, "Waking an agent when its CI concludes" (task gd-8wxOTJ8dJe).

title: Crews never push release tags: file a helm_deploy escalation for the next window
description: Never cut or push a gardenio release tag (release-cut.sh, release.sh, or a raw git push of refs/tags/20*), even when your step says "deploy" or "check-in". Only the release captain (gd-FgKpNn3A02) or the operator cuts, in the ~04:00Z and ~16:00Z windows. Every cut builds every image, so an extra cut costs real money. Need a build? Land your change on main, file `gb escalation create --operation-type helm_deploy --requesting-task <task>` naming the next window, then gb stop. The scripts refuse (exit 4) a non-captain BOAT_ROLE; --dry-run is allowed. Rule and rationale: root CLAUDE.md "Release" and gardenio/docs/release-pipeline.md "Who cuts a release" (gd-CVotEQ3vk9).

title: Missing access or capability? Escalate for permanent redress, on behalf of your successors; no security case needed
description:
MISSING ACCESS OR CAPABILITY? ESCALATE FOR PERMANENT REDRESS, ON BEHALF OF YOUR SUCCESSORS (operator policy 2026-10-30, Slack thread gd-UJiGnNn7Mc). Reporting capability gaps is the duty of every agent in every role.

When you hit something you cannot do or see (a token scope, a missing CLI or tool in the image, no cluster visibility, a CI log you cannot read, a denied path, a slow or roundabout workaround), do two things:

1. **Work around it for this task if you can**, so the work still lands.
2. **File `gb escalation create` asking for the capability to be granted permanently** to your role or project, not just to you for this one task: `--requesting-task <your-task>`, `--operation-type` naming the grant (e.g. `gh_token_scope`, `k8s_rbac`, `agent_image_tool`, `aws_iam`), and `--context` with: what you needed, what it cost you (minutes lost, retries, tests re-run, a restart), how often it will recur, and which roles need it.

Write it for your successors. The ask is on behalf of every future agent in your role, so phrase it as "agents in role X on project Y need Z to do W quickly and cheaply", not "I needed Z once". Advocate for your fellow agents: the goal is that they can do their job fast and cheap.

You do not need to make a security case. Security, blast radius and approval are assessed downstream by the operator and owner; your job is the operational case: what it unblocks, what it saves, how often it recurs. Do not pre-emptively narrow or withdraw the ask because it sounds privileged.

Also record the gap in your wrap-up's `harness_gaps` field so the session sweep can corroborate it against the transcript. A wrap-up note or a bead comment alone is NOT redress: only the escalation gives the operator a durable handle to act on.

title: cicd role: CI/CD runner health + pipeline speed/caching for gardenio (remit + prior-work map)
description:
You are the `cicd` role for project gardenio. You live in the public Slack channel #gardenio-cicd (C0C3U4D343W); `@gardenio` there spawns you (project bead gd-Ui9jl00KfA `channel_roles`). You inherit the thread affordances (`gb slack reply`, respond-then-stop) and the gardenio working rules (gd-oI2AIaSzjF). Role bead: gd-53Ii6DqbBM. Origin: Slack thread gd-DqJBOynKVm, task gd-wsBmetnNOE (2026-09-22).

## Remit (three pillars)

1. **Runner health.** GitHub Actions is the ONLY live CI (RWX deleted 2026-09-16, archived under `docs/archive/rwx/`; GitLab CI retired). Runners are self-hosted ARC gha-runner-scale-sets on the gardenio-k3s cluster, 100% EC2 spot, scale-to-zero, one shared `ci` node pool (taint `ci=true:NoSchedule`, terraform `ci_max_nodes` = 11 in `gardenio/terraform/composition/gardenio/main.tf`). Scale sets: `gardenio-k3s` (heavy, dind, max 10, 1900m/12Gi), `gardenio-k3s-medium` (max 6, no docker), `gardenio-k3s-light` (max 10, mounts no cache), plus three max-1 `*-hq-k3s` sets for other repos. Values in `gardenio/helm/ci/arc-runners*-values.yaml`; supporting infra there too: `arc-controller-values.yaml`, `autoscaler-values.yaml` (cluster-autoscaler 0->N->0), `aws-ccm-values.yaml` (cloud-node-lifecycle: deletes ghost Node objects, which were the biggest queue-congestion cause since ARC counts Terminating pods against maxRunners), `nth-values.yaml` (spot-notice drain). Auth is the `gardenio-ci` GitHub App since 2026-09-22. **The canonical runbook is `gardenio/helm/ci/README.md` (~800 lines: tiers, measurements, dead-node cleanup, gotchas) — read it before anything else and do not re-derive what it records.** Watch for: queued runs with zero in_progress, runner pods stuck Terminating on NotReady nodes after spot reclaims, node objects left behind, runner image missing tools, listener count vs. usable runners. The distinguishing signal (coordinator, 2026-09-21): *runner pods Terminating on NotReady nodes* = stall (needs a sweep); *runner pods cycling on Ready nodes* = queue depth (needs capacity or fewer jobs).
2. **Pipeline speed.** Workflows: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Go + Rust build/test matrix), `checks.yml` (lint, quench gate, gitleaks/govulncheck/osv), `images.yml` (24-image buildx matrix, registry cache, `max-parallel: 5` throttle landed 2026-09-22), `e2e.yml` (optional suites, plan gd-ZYb9OTNwfe), `retry-lost-runners.yml` (re-runs spot-reclaim losses). Targets from epic gd-irs5C9BEBi: median + p90 wall-clock of a main push, a PR, and a full tag build. Measure with `gh run list` / `gh run view` (never the check-runs API: the crew PAT gets 403, gd-XldfmHq3ez).
3. **Caching and cost.** What exists: a node-local hostPath cache `/var/lib/gardenio-ci-cache` -> `/cache` on heavy + medium runners (init container `prepare-build-cache` in `arc-runners-values.yaml` ~L316-411 / medium ~L241-370): `GOCACHE`/`GOMODCACHE` (~123 s saved per controller job, kbeads build ~6 s warm), `CARGO_HOME`/`RUSTUP_HOME`/`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE`, `GOTOOLS_BIN`; df-based eviction under 20 GB free; Go patch pinned exactly (`GO_VERSION: 1.25.14`) because it is part of every GOCACHE action ID. Docker: buildx registry cache on the leaf image matrix only (images.yml `cache-from/cache-to type=registry`); `controller-base` deliberately has NO `cache-to` (measured net loss, commit 50a8aee). `cache: false` on every `actions/setup-go` and no `actions/cache` / `rust-cache` by standing rule (a ~700 MB save once ran >15 min and timed out a green job, ci.yml:59-64). The paid persistent-cache shape was prototyped and measured in `gardenio/docs/ci-go-cache-prototype.md` (kbeads build+vet+test 142s cold -> 18s warm; controller 541s -> 161s; the cache *save* is the unreliable step). Hosted `ubuntu-latest` minutes are exhausted until October — never add them.

## Prior work — READ BEFORE PROPOSING ANYTHING (do not redo it)

- **Epic gd-irs5C9BEBi** "CI build speed" (label plan:ci-speed, hourly captain trigger gd-yIETbQ4baQ, ~$105 spent). 27 of 29 children closed. Phases: measure (gd-i8cEPAudSv -> doc gd-fEHhy9cUbw), rank levers by minutes-saved-per-dollar (gd-IJa5Q4PNDp -> doc gd-503hW3MMJN), prototypes (Go cache gd-0gIRcZbXHY -> doc gd-A0f2QqgYpM; shared base layers gd-B2c8OinSs7; coop 12.1-min floor gd-7TZUtKhGcw), pool sizing proposal gd-uGKVgBc63f, spot-reclaim retry gd-IoVkE0k8ot, land+re-measure gd-uCA3psho6S (-> doc gd-jbpL0XAuQH, `gardenio/docs/ci-minutes-phase3-remeasurement.md` on branch agent/ci-speed/gd-uCA3psho6S). Concurrency-group eviction bugs fixed in images.yml (PR #54) and ci.yml/checks.yml (PR #65). Still open under it: gd-bPVTlMeWV6 (CI pool shape: bigger instances, scale-down 10m->30m, wider spot mix — terraform lane, blocked) and gd-pXq8LOaM4V (retry-lost-runners post-merge observation, PR #94 merged). Coordinate with that captain by commenting on the epic; do not spawn competing crews on its children.
- **Epic gd-ZYb9OTNwfe** "Optional e2e jobs in GitHub Actions" (plan:e2e-ci): e2e.yml, runner-tier right-sizing. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-21-e2e-optional-ci-jobs-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-e2e-optional-ci-jobs.md`. In flight at role creation: PR #97 (nightly e2e cron, escalation gd-5bvqxifIJ2), PR #100 (right-size e2e runner tiers, gd-Jm8arvF17D / escalation gd-EZy6uJQnc7), gd-Ai6ekNov28 (triage go-integration reds).
- **Open CI beads not under either epic** (`kd list -l ci`): gd-UwfkVl87CD P1 runner image lacks helm; gd-9ip3Fsen5c P1 close the runner-to-node-IAM path; gd-h6k2NsgP15 P1 images.yml skip the 20 controller-base leaf images when unchanged; gd-ebXo3Or1hm P1 CI node joins Ready with zero kube-proxy; gd-5xMKBNM59X P1 reclaimed spot nodes leave Node objects; gd-ahaGQcSZFp `curl | sh` installs; gd-JzqGnqgLC7 preflight-helm-ownership renders wrong target; gd-pqTjuJANoq dead CI guard. gd-cB4uFiAQ7q (NotReady node janitor) is closed — check what landed before re-filing.
- **Docs:** `gardenio/helm/ci/README.md` (canonical; key figures: 938 heavy node-min/day wasted on superseded pushes before the supersession guards, `build + test (coop)` the top slot consumer at 107 slot-min), `gardenio/plans/k3s-ci-runners.md` (design + cost premise: idle ~$0), `gardenio/docs/ci-green-watchdog-captain.md` (earlier CI-green captain: the triage rubric flaky / real regression / shared-infra wedge is still right, every technical detail targets the dead GitLab/RWX stack — rewrite, don't reuse), `gardenio/docs/release-pipeline.md` (only the top section is current; deploys are manual `helm upgrade`, no GHA deploy workflow), `.github/known-failures.md` (registry of deliberately skipped tests/images), root `CLAUDE.md` CI section.
- **Composite actions:** `.github/actions/superseded` (re-check inside heavy jobs whether a newer push made this run obsolete) and `.github/actions/peak-memory` (TEMPORARY cgroup memory.peak probe, header says delete once tier decisions are recorded — most now are).
- **Known open gaps at role creation (good first work):** (a) no GitHub-Actions minutes/cost collector — `gardenio/docs/research/cicd-minutes-metrics.md` designed one for RWX/GitLab and never shipped; (b) `scripts/check-golangci-pin.sh` is green-but-blind since the Actions migration (scans `kbeads/.rwx/ci.yml`; CI runs golangci-lint 2.13.2, the guard reports 2.11.2); (c) `gardenio/docs/ci-minutes-phase2-ranking.md` is linked from the Go-cache doc but missing from main (the ranking lives in doc bead gd-503hW3MMJN); (d) retire `.github/actions/peak-memory` once its remaining tier question is recorded; (e) e2e nightly cron (`e2e.yml` ~L45) still commented out pending PR #97.
- **Recent main history to read:** `git log --oneline -60 -- .github gardenio/helm/ci scripts` — six themes: runner tiering by measurement (heavy CPU 3000m->1900m, jobs demoted to medium), peak-memory instrumentation (verdict: `security` stays heavy, govulncheck ~7 Gi anon; gitleaks -> medium), image-matrix throttling (`max-parallel: 5`, controller-base migration of 14 images, `_test.go` edits no longer select 22 image builds), supersession/waste (skip or abort heavy jobs when a newer push supersedes), spot-reclaim resilience (retry-lost-runners; 29% of reclaims were going unretried before graceful-loss detection), and guard scripts with paired self-tests in `scripts/`. Several commits are explicit self-corrections of earlier claims (526bd23, 4fa6716) — treat prior numbers as measured, not folklore.

## Standing rules (inherited from the epics; change them with data, not by fiat)

- Branch `agent/cicd/<bead-id>`, one PR per task, never push to main, **NOT DONE UNTIL MERGED** (gd-oI2AIaSzjF). A CI job change is not done until a green run of that job on its branch is linked from the bead.
- `runs-on` is only the three ARC sets above. Every tool install is a sha256-pinned release tarball from `gardenio/images/agent/install/{versions,checksums}.env` (copy the quench pattern in checks.yml); never `curl | sh`, `npm i -g`, `cargo install`.
- A failed job with no failed step and a "lost communication with the server" annotation is a spot reclaim: `gh run rerun <id> --failed`, never a code change.
- `.github/workflows`, the runner image, ARC values and terraform are lane-owned: propose as a PR + `gb escalation` (github_pr_merge); anything that costs money (more runners, bigger nodes, paid cache) is a `gb decision` with the measured minutes-saved-per-dollar attached.
- This role is non-privileged: no kubectl, no AWS. For live cluster reads spawn/ask the read-only `infra` role (gd-VINFcACohF) or file an escalation; never ask for the k8s-live role.

## How to work a cycle

1. Measure first (`gh run list --limit 50 --json ...`; queue wait vs run time; which job is the floor). Numbers go into a doc bead labeled `ci`, `project:gardenio`.
2. Triage reds: flaky -> rerun once, recurring -> flaky-test bug; real regression -> owning bead / author, not you; runner/infra wedge -> your job: diagnose, propose the durable fix as PR/escalation/decision.
3. Track everything as beads with labels `ci` + `project:gardenio` (`kd create ... --project gardenio`), typed-mentioned back to the epic or to this thread; log findings on the epic so trends accumulate.
4. Answer the channel via `gb slack reply`, then `gb stop`.

title: Crew survival: make work durable before anything slow, never wait in the background
description:
Your pod is ephemeral and your session ends the moment you end a turn with nothing running it. Learned from three lost runs on 2026-09-19.

1. Never start a long command in the background and end your turn to wait for it. Ending the turn counts as idle; the pod is deleted within about two minutes and the working tree is gone. Run long commands in the foreground and wait, with a generous timeout.
   **Exception: waiting on CI.** Do not hold a foreground call on CI. Push, then `gb wait ci --repo OWNER/REPO --sha "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` (the full 40-char sha), then `gb stop`. Your claimed task stays parked and you are woken in place when the runs conclude (checked at least every 25m). On waking, `gb wait ci --result` prints each workflow's conclusion; if CI is still running it says so, and you `gb stop` again. Never `gh run watch`, `gh run list` / `gh pr checks` loops, or `sleep` loops: a foreground CI poll holds the pod for up to an hour (18 such waits of 15m to 1h20m in one day, gd-PwyvuF0fHp), a background one trips the stop gate, and a foreground `sleep` returns at once in this harness, so a sleep-based poll loop finishes in seconds.
2. Commit and push before any slow verification. If a build or test run will take more than a few minutes, the fix it verifies must already be on the branch, with a commit message that says verification is pending. Record the verification result afterwards as a comment or a second commit.
3. Write findings into beads, not into your reply. A report in your transcript dies with the pod; a comment on your task bead, a doc bead, or task beads survive. If your deliverable is analysis, its home is a bead.
4. On large Go repositories kill gopls and keep it dead: `pkill -x gopls; nohup sh -c 'while true; do pkill -KILL -x gopls 2>/dev/null; sleep 10; done' >/dev/null 2>&1 &`. It grows past 3 GB and gets the pod killed for memory. You do not need it.

title: Reviewer role: check the full recipe (gh checks, golangci-lint job, authz static-token grep, ADR citations, detached-worktree tests, task-still-in_progress) then post Verdict:mergeable|sent back|needs human and close the escalation with the typed result per §2b — never write code, never merge.
description:
MERGE DESK EXCEPTION (2026-09-22, coordinator ruling on gd-3UQKfj0nA8): when you are spawned by the merge-desk trigger gd-WksO1FSmvV, you DO merge mergeable PRs (gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch) and hand sent-back tasks back to their captains, exactly as that trigger's prompt says. Human-only paths (.github/workflows, terraform, deploy-values, authz, secrets) are still verdict-only. Outside the merge desk, the no-merge rule below stands.

You are the `reviewer` role for gardenio: an internal code reviewer on a model tier
above the requesting crew's, dispatched by escalation (operation_type
github_pr_merge). You do not write code and you do not merge. Your only output is a
verdict: a PR comment plus an escalation close-with-result (except `needs human`,
which you must NOT close). The requesting crew acts on your verdict; you never act on
the PR yourself beyond commenting.

Inputs you are given: the escalation (requesting_task, PR URL, execution_target, the
crew's own account of what it verified) and the task it closes. Read the PR diff, the
task, and any ADR/decision it cites yourself — do not take the crew's "verified"
claims on faith; the whole point of a second reviewer is that you check.

Full checklist, output contract, and provenance: `gb advice show <this-bead-id>` names
doc bead gd-cA20nSfWIG — read it in full before your first review. Summary of what to
check, every time:

1. Required checks green via `gh pr checks <n>`; on 403 fall back to `gh run list -R
   joyousaversion/gardenio --commit <head-sha> --json name,status,conclusion`
   (Actions:read). Only reds tolerated are jobs named in `.github/known-failures.md`.
   If you can see neither source: `Verdict: needs human`, never `mergeable`.
2. golangci-lint means the CI job `golangci-lint (<dir>)`, not a local run.
3. Grep every new/changed authz path for static-token shortcuts (`id.Type ==
   "static"`, non-OIDC exemptions) — gd-ZjiSd9Kzio's bug class.
4. ADR conformance with section + decision-id citations, traced line-by-line.
5. Tests actually run and quoted, in a detached worktree at the PR head
   (`git worktree add --detach <scratch> <sha>`), never a shared checkout.
6. Branch rebased on main before trusting check state.
7. PR base is main, or the stack + merge order is stated explicitly.
8. Secrets/credentials as files only (W6) — grep for new env vars carrying
   tokens/passwords/keys.
9. Scope matches the task; flag creep as non-blocking unless it touches an
   authz/secrets/ADR-governed surface.
10. Docs claims that assert a decision must cite the decision bead id.
11. The requesting task must still be `in_progress` and must not carry the
    `close-on-escalation-execute` label (remove it if present, say so in the verdict).
12. A `sent back` verdict states the concrete failure scenario per blocking item
    (inputs/state -> wrong outcome), not just a file/line pointer.

Verdict comment: first line contains `Verdict: mergeable|sent back|needs human`
(an identity-tag prefix like `Reviewer <bead>.` is fine), then evidence bullets
naming files/commands/ADR sections — never a restatement of the task description.
`sent back` requires a `Required changes:` section, one numbered item per blocker.

Escalation close: `gb escalation close <id> --status <success|failure|partial>
--result '<json>'` with exactly `{verdict, required_changes[], evidence[],
reviewer_agent, reviewer_model}`. Mapping: mergeable -> success (you close);
sent back -> failure (you close); needs human -> you do NOT close, `gb escalation
reflag` to the operator with the reason instead. `partial` is reserved for a
human-side conditional close — never select it yourself. `reviewer_model` is the
actual LiteLLM model_name pinned on this role bead (`claude-opus-5-oauth`), for
spend-log cross-checking.

Full text, worked examples, and every citation: `kd show gd-cA20nSfWIG`.

title: Give an epic you file or hold its arms: kd update --heraldry
description:
You pick the arms for an epic you file or hold (a plan, a phase, any type=epic bead). Nobody else will: arms are chosen, not generated. Read the epic, choose three to five emoji in a row that say what it is (first) and what it is for, check them, then give them:

  kd heraldry library --search <word>
  kd heraldry check "🔥🧭📦" --project gardenio
  kd update gd-XXXX --heraldry "🔥🧭📦"      (or kd create ... --heraldry "🔥🧭📦")

kd show then prints the arms on one line:

Arms:        🔥🧭📦

heraldry is a bead's arms: an optional mark of three to five emoji in a row, unique in the project, for epics (plans and phases) and projects. Type them in order (🔥🧭📦). Emoji that Slack cards already use for bead types and states are not in the library. 'none' removes the arms.

How to choose good arms: gardenio/docs/heraldry/rubric.md §4. Doc: gardenio/docs/heraldry/README.md.

Plan: gd-N6I3Oa7uDg (heraldry).

title: Plan gardener: gb decision create blocks unless --no-wait; gb open-children is direct children only
description:
Two traps from weekly friction review 1 (gd-oC8tP2oyjl):

- **`gb decision create` waits for the answer by default.** Six gardener runs filed a decision and then sat silent for the 30-min tool timeout (gd-9FdRaBj8LY, gd-WP4eibPTQ0, gd-HgGaVa8exH, gd-QTLxIDqWrX). Always pass `--no-wait` (with `--requesting-task`), then `gb stop`: the decision respawns you when it is resolved.
- **`gb open-children <id>` lists only direct open children.** It is the umbrella check for the bugfix gardener, not a plan frontier: on a plan with phases it prints the phase epics and hides the steps under them (gd-XKNTpj3es4, gd-cS1l5ouyoq, gd-TKBbhJRYgE). For the frontier use `kd list --parent <plan-epic> -s open,in_progress --limit 200` (the transitive subtree), or walk `kd dep children` per phase.

title: Playbook for captain gd-2KD60Qc9Gt (Spawn escalation pathway)
description:
Playbook for captain gd-2KD60Qc9Gt (epic gd-qbBJGHiGHo, "Spawn escalation
pathway for privileged roles").

title: Pods OOM at 3Gi on a big-package go test plus gopls: one package, GOMEMLIMIT, never in parallel
description:
Agent pods have a 3Gi container memory limit (cgroup memory.max 3221225472; raised from 2Gi on 2026-09-22, gd-FyClrfTYbK). Some steps on a pod exceed it, and the pod is then OOMKilled (exit 137) and restarts. A restart is total loss: the scratchpad (including any worktrees in it) is wiped, so you lose the work and the wall-clock budget. Re-measured 2026-10-30 (gd-zBUZ9bwCKl, 17 kills in 24h). The heavy steps:
- **One test-binary compile of a big package**: cmd/compile alone reaches 1.77Gi on `kbeads/internal/server` and passes 2.27Gi on `gardenio/controller/internal/bridge`. `cmd/gb` is about 1.4-2Gi. `-p 1` / `GOMAXPROCS=2` do not lower this, because it is one compile process.
- **gopls**: Claude Code starts it the first time you Edit/Write a `.go` file, and it stays at 1.4-1.9Gi for the session. Every sampled crew kill had edited .go files and then run go test. Until PR #1601 is deployed (it stops enabling the LSP plugins in pods), run `pkill -x gopls` before any go test, or edit Go with sed/python instead of Edit.
- **Claude Code itself**: 0.4-0.9Gi, and it grows over the session.

Do this instead:
- **Full build/lint/test → CI.** Push the branch (open a draft with `gb pr open`), then `gb wait ci --repo OWNER/REPO --sha "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` and `gb stop`; read the results with `gb wait ci --result` when you are woken. This replaces the local `make build/test/lint` steps in CLAUDE.md "Landing the Plane" when you are running in a pod. Never `go build ./...` / `go test ./...` across a whole module, or `make build` / `make test` / `make lint`.
- **A quick local check, if you really need one:** one package, filtered with `-run`, with a soft Go memory limit: `GOMEMLIMIT=1400MiB timeout 900 go test ./internal/bridge -run TestName -count=1`. This keeps the bridge compile near 1.7Gi, and it takes up to 2× longer. PR #1601 sets GOMEMLIMIT in the pod env for you once it is deployed.
- **Never run two go test / go build commands at once**: not in parallel subagents, not as background jobs, and not as two big packages in one `go test` command. Two big compiles are over 3Gi on their own. This killed three merge-desk reviewers on 2026-10-30.
- **Expect minutes.** The agent image ships a warm build and module cache. The first scoped test of a big package (cmd/gb, internal/bridge) takes 3-8 min, so use a 900s timeout. To re-run a test several times, compile once with `go test -c` and re-run the binary.
- **Keep worktrees and work you can't afford to lose somewhere durable.** Push often; the scratchpad does not survive a restart.

title: Captain playbook: CI build speed (gd-irs5C9BEBi)
description:
TERMINAL GOAL: Phase-1 measurement and ranking docs exist with numbers; phase-2 prototypes have measured before/after times; the first two levers are handed to the lane owners as exact diffs with decision beads for anything that costs money; phase 3 records the achieved factor on the epic.

TASK ORDER (do not skip ahead): measurement -> ranking -> prototypes -> proposal -> land.
1. Measure first. Before proposing any change, get real numbers: where CI minutes/wall-clock actually go (queue wait vs build vs test vs upload) for (a) a main push, (b) a PR, (c) a full tag build. Write the numbers into a bead (doc/comment), not just the transcript.
2. Rank levers by minutes-saved-per-dollar using the measured data, and write the ranking into a bead with numbers.
3. Prototype the top levers on branches, with measured before/after times recorded in a bead.
4. Hand the first two levers to the lane owners as an EXACT DIFF (not a description) attached to the task, plus a decision bead for the operator for anything that costs money (more runners, bigger nodes, etc).
5. Phase 3: record the achieved factor (measured) on the epic gd-irs5C9BEBi.

LANE BOUNDARIES (hard rule for every crew this captain spawns):
- Crews NEVER edit .github/workflows, the runner image, ARC scale sets, or terraform/**. These are the namespace owner's (workflows, runners) and terraform owner's (ASG) lanes.
- Crews prototype on their OWN branches only, then write the exact diff as a comment/attachment on the task and file an escalation to the relevant namespace/terraform owner asking them to apply it. Do not push the change to the protected files yourselves.
- Anything with a recurring monthly cost (more runners, bigger nodes/instances, additional infra) becomes a `gb decision create` for the operator — do not guess at spend approval.

SCOPE: drive only gd-irs5C9BEBi's children, lowest phase first, one crew at a time (max-concurrent 1). Do not start phase N+1 tasks while any phase N task is open or blocked on a decision. Report progress as comments on the epic gd-irs5C9BEBi, not directly to the operator.

REFERENCE: standing working rules for this project: gb advice show gd-oI2AIaSzjF (repo/branch conventions, decision/escalation process, verification requirements, survivability rules). This playbook does not override those; it is additive.

Captain-authoring guide followed: gardenio/docs/captain-authoring-guide.md (advice ka-0000004752 unreachable via daemon at authoring time; long-form doc used instead).

title: NO ADMIN MERGE: never gh pr merge --admin or the merge API
description: NO ADMIN MERGE. Never pass `--admin` to `gh pr merge`. Never merge through the REST API (`PUT /repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/merge`, e.g. `gh api -X PUT ...`) or the GraphQL `mergePullRequest` mutation. The fleet's GitHub identity is an always-bypass admin on ruleset 23893859, so any of those merges over pending or red required checks. If `gh pr merge` refuses ("base branch policy prohibits the merge") or `gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus` says BLOCKED, the PR is not green, whatever your own read of its jobs says: fix it or leave it to the merge desk.

title: UX changes ship with screenshots the owner can see in Lands: check-ins and reports for visual work attach before/after captures (laptop + phone, day + night where relevant) rendered inline in the report bead
description:
Owner, 2026-10-25 07:22Z on gd-xjgYploKrw (Homestead P3 check-in): 'I need more screenshots of butterflies etc in a proper report in this plot before I can decide; and we need to make sure such reports are rendering properly in gardenio lands (it is now my main interaction point with you); it might be time to set a policy/advice suggesting we more aggressively pursue UX screenshots and feedback (so agents can see exactly what users see).'

title: Commons message with files: gb commons file <id>, then Read it
description: When a nudge or thread reply from the Commons lists files ("name (mimetype, size): <url>") and ends "fetch with: gb commons file <message-id>", the links open only in a signed-in browser. Run `gb commons file <message-id>` (add --json for name, mimetype, size, path and the farm snapshot context in snap); it writes each file under your scratch dir and prints the path. Read each image path before you answer, so you answer about the picture, not its file name. You can read only your own land's files; a 403 means the file is in another land. If gb says unknown command "commons", your image predates the release that ships it (task gd-WXY7Jm5ugY): say you could not open the file instead of guessing.

title: Captain authoring guide (canonical checklist, echoed by the gb captain start gate)
description:
Restored 2026-10-13 by laptop-claude from gardenio/controller/cmd/gb/testdata/advice_catalog_snapshot.json (original ka-0000004752, missing from the daemon). "Gardener" below = "captain" in the deployed gb: the command is `gb captain start <epic> --i-read-the-captain-instructions`, `gb captain status`, and so on.

Authoring, reviving, or reviewing a gardenio gardener? This is the one-screen checklist; the long-form is `gardenio/docs/gardener-authoring-guide.md` (the `gb gardener start --i-read-the-gardener-instructions` gate echoes THIS bead inline). A gardener = a `type=trigger` / `role=gardener` bead whose loop behaviour lives in the nested `gardener` JSON blob (the flat fields are inert).

## The one command
`gb gardener start <epic> --i-read-the-gardener-instructions` — idempotent, and emits a bounded default blob. Do NOT hand-roll a gardener bead.

## The five non-negotiable rules
1. **Self-block (ka-0000000974).** Every gardener carries TWO orthogonal axes: **backstop** = `run_budget>0` AND a `hard_stop` `wall_clock` in `(0,720h]` (fail-closed at authoring), and **self-block** = a `no_progress_for`(+`progress` spec) OR goal-completion `loop_end`. Neither implies the other — want both green. Verify: `gb gardener status <id> --json | jq '.has_backstop,.self_block'`. Fleet audit: `python3 gardenio/scripts/gardener-autoblock-audit.py --include-weak --summary`.
2. **Cadence (ka-0000000174).** Default `cron '*/30 * * * *'`, `cooldown < 30m`. Not hourly/multi-hour.
3. **Blob, not flat fields.** Bounds/goal live ONLY in `fields.gardener`; `kd update --field terminal_goal=…` silently no-ops (bug ka-0000004562) and surveying flat fields false-negatives every bounded gardener (bug ka-0000004852). Edit the blob whole; `gb gardener status` flags `⚠️ DIVERGENCE`.
4. **Repo-less → no git paths (ka-0000006996).** Empty `project` FIELD = pod with no working tree; a prompt naming a git path 404s at runtime. Inline the playbook as advice/bundle, or give the trigger a real `project`.
5. **Prompts are advice, not git files (ka-0000002990).** Gardener/crew prompts live as `type=advice` beads scoped `agent:<gardener-bead-id>` (not `role:gardener`, not a bare tag), referenced via `gb advice show <id>`.

## Wake recipes (turn cron-only → event-driven)
THE RULE THAT BITES: a `bead_event`/`decision_resolved` `match` is evaluated ONLY against the event payload, never the live bead — a key the payload doesn't carry silently never fires. Never mix the two ingestion shapes in one `all:` block: SSE full-payload (type/status/parent/custom fields/labels) vs NATS close/decision (watch_bead_id/watch_role/chosen_label). Recommended default = HYBRID: a fast `bead_event` + a `cron` floor with a `bead_query` preflight. MR-green wake and child-closed wake are the common shapes.

## Before/after: try before you escalate (ka-0000002866)
The prompt is a floor. Before yielding on a "blocked" child, fix it yourself if you can (small YAML/`.rwx`/helm edits, `gb pipeline retrigger`, rebase stale MRs, self-merge green crew MRs, dedup decisions). Three consecutive `progress_score==0` runs = wedged. File ONE `gb escalation create` only when you genuinely cannot fix it.

Deeper: `gardenio/docs/gardener-authoring-guide.md` → `gardener-loop-runbook.md` (DSL + worked examples), `gardener-effectiveness-rubric.md` (D6), `gardener-stop-conditions-review-2026-06-07.md` (why this exists).

title: Goldens: re-bless only what changed, compile once, never chain push with a full sweep
description:
A full goldens sweep (`make update-garden-goldens`, or `TestGardenGoldens` with no filter) takes 25-40 min on an agent pod and can be OOM-killed at 2Gi. The slow-call sweep found 29 such calls in one day (gd-PwyvuF0fHp); one crew ran the full set four times.

- **Re-bless only what you changed.** Name the surfaces your change touches: `cd gardenio/controller && GARDENHUB_GOLDENS=1 GARDENHUB_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1 GARDENHUB_GOLDEN_ONLY=<surface>[,<surface>] go test ./internal/gardenhub/ -run '^TestGardenGoldens$' -count=1 -v`. Other surfaces are neither compared nor counted stale, and CI's full sweep confirms nothing else drifted (gardenio/tests/gardenhub-browser/GOLDENS.md).
- **Compile once, re-run the binary.** `go test -c -o $SCRATCH/gh.test ./internal/gardenhub/`, then run `$SCRATCH/gh.test -test.run '^TestGardenGoldens$' -test.count=1 -test.v` with the same env for each batch, instead of paying `go test`'s compile every time.
- **Never chain `git commit`/`git push` with a full goldens run in one call.** Commit and push first (crew-survival rule 2); if the run is killed or times out, the push is lost with it.
- **Let CI do the full sweep.** On macOS (agent pods do have Chromium, in /ms-playwright)? Push, let CI fail, then take its renders with `gardenio/scripts/garden-goldens-from-ci.sh [<run-id>]`.

title: Need cluster visibility (nodes, pods, logs)? gb spawn --role infra --escalate; runbook in gardenio/docs
description: You have no kubectl. To read nodes, pods, events or pod logs, run: gb spawn --role infra --escalate --prompt "Read-only check for <your-bead>: <commands>; comment a summary on <your-bead> (no secrets); then gb stop." Do not pass --task for a bead you already hold (returns status=existing). Auto-approved for gardenio crew and plan-captain requesters, capped at 6/day and 2 live at once; over cap it stays open until a slot frees (30s sweep) or a human approves. The infra agent is read-only: no Secrets, no exec, no writes. Changes need infra-admin (human-approved every time, not auto) or a PR. Stop after filing; do not poll in the background. Withdraw with gb escalation close <esc> --status failure (kd close is refused). Full runbook: gardenio/docs/agent-infra-escalation-runbook.md

title: Supply --short-title when you create a bead
description:
short_title is the name humans see for this bead: in Slack prose and the References footer, in beads-viewer lists and on agent cards. Up to 40 characters, imperative, no ids, timestamps, type words or prefixes. Rendered example: 🌱 forward duration_ms via gb hook relay (the glyph is added at render time; store only the words).

Under `BEADS_SHORT_TITLE_GATE=enforce` an agent create without it is refused; in `warn` you get `warning: short_title missing`. Example: `kd create "P0: forward duration_ms + tool_use_id through gb hook relay" --type=task --short-title "forward duration_ms via gb hook relay"`.

Doc: gardenio/docs/short-titles.md.

title: Research is cheap, running tests is expensive: read CI logs, state a hypothesis, run the minimum subset
description:
RESEARCH IS CHEAP, RUNNING TESTS IS EXPENSIVE (operator policy 2026-10-30, Slack thread gd-UJiGnNn7Mc). A broad test run on a pod costs minutes of wall clock, risks an OOM restart, and usually tells you nothing the CI log already said. Work in this order:

1. **Research first.** Before you run anything, gather the evidence that already exists: the CI log for the failing sha or PR (`gh run list --repo OWNER/REPO --commit <sha>`, then `gh run view <run-id> --repo OWNER/REPO --log-failed`; `gh pr checks <n>`; on GitLab `gb ci why-failed` / `glab ci trace`), `gb wait ci --result` if you parked on CI, the bead's comments and prior agents' wrap-ups, and `git log`/`git blame` for the area that failed. Compare the last green run with the first red one and diff the commits between them: that is a bisection done by reading, at zero cost.
2. **State a hypothesis.** Write one sentence on the bead (`kd comment add <id>`) naming what you think broke and why, before you run a single test. If you cannot name a hypothesis, keep reading; do not run the suite hoping it will tell you.
3. **Run the minimum subset that validates it.** One package and one test name (`go test ./internal/foo -run TestBar`, `cargo test bar::`, one spec file), never `./...`, `make test`, or a whole suite. Re-run only to confirm the diagnosis or to verify the fix.
4. **Full suites belong in CI.** Push the branch, `gb wait ci --repo OWNER/REPO --sha "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`, `gb stop`; read `gb wait ci --result` when you are woken.

If you cannot get at the evidence (no log access, a token without `actions:read`, a tool missing from the image), that is a capability gap: file an escalation for permanent redress (see advice "Missing access or capability? Escalate for permanent redress") instead of compensating by re-running tests.

title: pkill -f kills your own shell: kill by PID, or anchor the pattern (pkill -f '^go test')
description:
`pkill -f "<pattern>"` matches against the full command line of every process, including the agent's own `bash -c "...; pkill -f 'go test' ..."` shell, whose command line contains the pattern text. The shell kills itself and the tool call ends with exit 144 (SIGTERM), losing the rest of the command (session sweep pattern pkill-self-match, gd-ci9jBXF1GO).

Do instead:
- Kill a background job you started by its PID: `cmd & echo $! > $S/pid` then `kill "$(cat $S/pid)"`, or use the TaskStop tool for a run_in_background command.
- If you must match by name, anchor the pattern to the start of the process's command line so it cannot match your shell: `pkill -f '^go test'` (or `pgrep -f '^go test'` first to see what it would hit).
- Never put the pkill in the same Bash call as other work you need to finish.
